📄 Iran and Iraq stress border security, counterterrorism cooperation

📌 Tehran, IRNA — Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and his Iraqi counterpart Fuad Hussein have emphasized the implementation of the agreements on border security and effectively countering terrorist movements.

During the meeting, which was held on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly session in New York, the two sides underlined the importance of safeguarding shared border security.
​
They reviewed cooperation between the two countries in economic, commercial, consular, and security fields.
​
Both ministers underscored that protecting their shared borders is of paramount importance, stressing the need to carry out the agreements already reached and to counter terrorist activity effectively.
​
Araghchi outlined the latest developments regarding the shipping situation in the Strait of Hormuz, including the understanding reached between Iran and Oman to designate safe routes for commercial shipping.
​
He noted that the existing insecurity in the Strait of Hormuz is solely due to the aggressive actions of the United States and the Israeli regime and that the return of security to this strait requires the cessation of US’ destabilizing actions.
​
Araghchi urged all countries in the region to adhere to the principle of good neighborliness, particularly preventing aggressor parties from using their territory and facilities to prepare and carry out illegal and aggressive actions against Iran.
​
Iran is determined to defend its sovereignty and national interests, he stated.

💬 Europe cannot claim support for law while backing US-Israeli aggression: Araghchi

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi says European countries cannot claim to support the rule of law and human rights while remaining indifferent to, or supporting, the US-Israeli military aggression against Iran.

Araghchi made the remarks during a meeting with Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen on Tuesday on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York.
​
The two foreign ministers discussed bilateral relations as well as regional and international developments.
​
Araghchi strongly criticized European countries’ double standards toward regional developments, particularly their silence regarding hostile US and Israeli actions against Iran.
​
He also recalled Iran’s responsible approach to diplomacy aimed at removing US pretexts over the nuclear issue, saying repeated US treaty violations and its pursuit of war were the main causes of insecurity in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz.
​
Araghchi stressed that restoring peace and stability in the region requires an end to US illegal and aggressive actions and respect for Iran’s national rights and interests.
​
Berendsen, for his part, stressed the importance of diplomacy and outlined the Netherlands’ views on current regional developments and interactions between Iran and Europe.
​
The 81st UN General Assembly is being held in New York from September 22 to 28.

Araghchi, who is in New York to attend the annual United Nations General Assembly, met with French Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot on Tuesday afternoon on the sidelines of the gathering. ​
Araghchi criticized France’s positions toward Iran and emphasized that the French embassy must comply with Iranian laws and regulations.
​
He also called France’s stance on regional developments, particularly its position regarding the US and Israeli military aggression against Iran, unacceptable.
​
Referring to France’s double standards on human rights, Araghchi said Paris could not claim concern for human rights while remaining silent over crimes against humanity by the United States and the Israeli regime against the Iranian people, including the killing of Iranian women and children.
​
He also criticized France for cooperating in the implementation of illegal US sanctions against the Iranian people.
​
Araghchi stressed that Iran seeks relations based on mutual respect and interests with all countries, including France, but will act firmly and decisively to defend its interests and national interests.
